description: The view turns by the Windows cursor's movement (GetCursorPos minus the last position, then SetCursorPos back to the window centre), read once a frame: Windows' pointer speed and acceleration (Enhance pointer precision) change how far a mouse movement turns, and a fast movement within one frame is cut short at the screen's edge before the recentre. Raw device counts are what the player moved.
evidence: The faithful IN_Frame (tests/differential/test_win_input.py) passes GetCursorPos's difference to CL_MouseEvent; the cursor is clipped to the window (ClipCursor in CL_MouseEvent) and recentred only after the read.

description: Mouse acceleration and smoothing in the game's own path: cl_mouseAccel adds (counts per millisecond) * cl_mouseAccel to the sensitivity, and m_filter averages this frame's movement with the last one's, which delays and blurs aim. Neither belongs in raw mouse aim.
evidence: src/client_mp/cl_input.cpp CL_GetMouseMovementWithSensitivity, matches the Store build: ((length / frame_msec) * cl_mouseAccel + sensitivity) * FOV scale; m_filter sums the two slots.

description: The yaw is never brought back into a turn's range: it grows with every turn the same way, and a float yaw of thousands of degrees has steps of 0.0001 degrees and more, so small mouse movements turn unevenly after long sessions.
evidence: CL_MouseMove subtracts the turn from clViewangles[1] with no wrap (src/client_mp/cl_input.cpp); nothing else in the mouse path wraps it.

description: The mouse's turn per count changes with the field of view and aiming down sights (cgameFOVSensitivityScale) and is in the game's own units (sensitivity * m_yaw), unlike the user's MW2019-style setting in degrees per count.
evidence: CL_GetMouseMovementWithSensitivity multiplies by cgameFOVSensitivityScale; CL_MouseMove by m_yaw / m_pitch.
